validated_results.title: Both serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and calcium levels may increase the risk of incident prostate cancer in Caribbean men of African ancestry.
validated_results.reason: Case-control study of Caribbean men reporting a multivariable-adjusted odds ratio for incident prostate cancer per unit increase in serum calcium.

extraction.comparison_type: continuous, per 0.1 nmol/L higher serum calcium
extraction.population: Men 40-80 years old with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed prostate cancer and controls

effect_size.excerpt: Multivariable-adjusted models showed a positive linear relationship between PCa and serum calcium (OR, 1.12; CI, 1.00-1.25 per 0.1 nmol/L). Serum 25(OH)D concentration also showed a positive association with PCa (OR, 1.23; CI, 1.01-1.49 per 10 ng/mL).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Multivariable-adjusted models showed a positive linear relationship between PCa and serum calcium (OR, 1.12; CI, 1.00-1.25 per 0.1 nmol/L).

design.excerpt: We examined these relationships in a case-control study of men 40-80 years old with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed PCa in Jamaica

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Mean serum calcium concentrations was higher among cases (2.32 ± 0.19 mmol/L) than controls

parallel_r3_gate_reasons: important quantitative evidence remains missing or invalid: cases, p_value, total_n

validated_results.journal: Journal of biological regulators and homeostatic agents

validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute

validated_results.title: Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Green Tea Catechins for Prostate Cancer Prevention.
validated_results.reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of a green tea catechin preparation reporting cumulative one-year prostate cancer incidence in both arms.

extraction.comparison_type: Polyphenon E (400 mg EGCG/day) versus placebo
extraction.population: Men with high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia (HGPIN) and/or atypical small acinar proliferation (ASAP)

sample_size.excerpt: We conducted a placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial of Polyphenon E (PolyE), a proprietary mixture of GTCs, containing 400 mg (-)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) per day, in 97 men with high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia (HGPIN) and/or atypical small acinar proliferation (ASAP).

cases.excerpt: No differences in the number of prostate cancer cases were observed: 5 of 49 (PolyE) versus 9 of 48 (placebo), P = 0.25.
cases.location: abstract; cases derived from reported group counts 5 + 9 = 14

comparison.excerpt: a comparison of the cumulative one-year prostate cancer rates on the two study arms

design.excerpt: We conducted a placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial of Polyphenon E (PolyE), a proprietary mixture of GTCs

timing.excerpt: Daily intake of a standardized, decaffeinated catechin mixture containing 400 mg EGCG per day for 1 year

parallel_r3_gate_reasons: JBI remains Fair after Claude R2
important quantitative evidence remains missing or invalid: ci_lower, ci_upper, effect_size, effect_type

validated_results.reason: The trial administered a decaffeinated green tea catechin extract (Polyphenon E) rather than tea consumption, so tea intake as an exposure is absent.
